propositions: Reconciler field asymmetry policies (removal gates, add-wins merging, link directions) are scattered across multiple call sites with no single declarative registry, allowing parity bugs to escape undetected.

A new declarative field contract registry module enumerates all reconciled fields with their symmetry class (bidirectional-roundtrip, add-wins, or one-way-with-propagation-gate) and references to their codecs/gates.

Property tests parameterized off the registry assert roundtrip identity for bidirectional fields, merge idempotence for add-wins fields, and gate consultation for one-way-gated fields through real call paths.
A coverage guard fails test collection if any field handled by inbound_differ/apply_inbound_records lacks a registry entry, enforcing declaration on new field addition.
The landed typed-transport hardening (cc77/Gerrit 1222-1225) provides the foundation for building property tests against the declared symmetry surface.
